_about: Paul's journeys rebuilt stop by stop from Acts. Places use the Bible Atlas coordinates. Steps happen 'at' a place in story order (return legs revisit places); 'by: sea' marks legs Acts describes as sailing.

set.note: Every city Acts 13-14 names is shown, including the return through the same churches. Roads and sea lanes between them are simplified.

steps.label: Sent off from Antioch
steps.copy: After fasting and prayer, the church sends off Barnabas and Saul, as the Holy Spirit directed.

steps.label: Down to the coast
steps.copy: They go down to Seleucia to sail for Cyprus.

steps.label: Salamis
steps.copy: They proclaim the word of God in the Jewish synagogues, with John as their helper.

steps.label: Paphos
steps.copy: Across the island, the sorcerer Elymas is struck blind and the proconsul Sergius Paulus believes.

steps.label: Perga
steps.copy: They sail to Perga in Pamphylia, where John leaves them and returns to Jerusalem.

steps.label: Pisidian Antioch
steps.copy: Paul preaches in the synagogue; many Gentiles believe, and opposition drives them out of the region.

steps.label: Iconium
steps.copy: A great number believe, but when a plot to stone them forms, they flee.

steps.label: Lystra
steps.copy: Paul heals a man who had never walked. The crowd calls them gods, then Paul is stoned and left for dead.

steps.label: Derbe
steps.copy: They preach the gospel in Derbe and make many disciples.

steps.label: Back to Lystra
steps.copy: They turn back to strengthen the disciples and urge them to remain in the faith.

steps.label: Back through Iconium
steps.copy: They encourage the believers in Iconium again.

steps.label: Elders for the churches
steps.copy: Back in Pisidian Antioch, they appoint elders in each church with prayer and fasting.

steps.label: Preaching in Perga
steps.copy: They pass through Pisidia and Pamphylia and speak the word in Perga.

steps.label: Attalia
steps.copy: They go down to the port of Attalia.

steps.label: Home to Antioch
steps.copy: They sail back to Antioch and tell the church how God opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.

set.note: Every city Acts 15:36-18:22 names on the way is shown, from Antioch to Corinth and back by sea. Roads between them are simplified.

steps.label: Paul and Silas set out
steps.copy: After a sharp disagreement over John Mark, Barnabas sails for Cyprus, and Paul takes Silas through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.

steps.label: Derbe
steps.copy: Paul comes back to Derbe.

steps.label: Lystra: Timothy joins
steps.copy: A disciple named Timothy joins them, and the churches grow stronger in the faith and larger every day.

steps.label: Troas
steps.copy: Kept from speaking in Asia and from entering Bithynia, they reach Troas, where Paul sees a vision of a man of Macedonia calling for help.

steps.label: Samothrace
steps.copy: They sail straight across to Samothrace.

steps.label: Neapolis
steps.copy: The next day they reach Neapolis, in Europe.

steps.label: Philippi
steps.copy: Lydia believes. Paul and Silas are beaten and jailed, sing hymns at midnight, and the jailer and his household are baptized.

steps.label: Thessalonica
steps.copy: By way of Amphipolis and Apollonia, they reach Thessalonica. Paul reasons from the Scriptures for three Sabbaths; some believe, and a mob sets the city in an uproar.

steps.label: Berea
steps.copy: The Bereans receive the word eagerly and examine the Scriptures every day.

steps.label: Athens
steps.copy: Distressed by the city's idols, Paul speaks at the Areopagus about the unknown God.

steps.label: Corinth
steps.copy: He makes tents with Aquila and Priscilla and stays a year and a half, teaching the word of God.

steps.label: Cenchreae
steps.copy: Paul has his hair cut because of a vow and sets sail for Syria.

steps.label: Ephesus
steps.copy: He reasons in the synagogue and promises to come back, if God wills.

steps.label: Caesarea
steps.copy: He lands at Caesarea and goes up to greet the church.

steps.label: Home to Antioch
steps.copy: Then he goes down to Antioch.

set.note: Every place Acts 18:23-21:17 names on the way is shown. 'Macedonia' and 'Greece' are regions in the text; Greece is placed at Corinth, where Paul most likely stayed.

steps.label: Setting out again
steps.copy: After some time in Antioch, Paul travels through Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.

steps.label: Ephesus
steps.copy: He teaches daily in the lecture hall of Tyrannus for two years, so that everyone in Asia hears the word of the Lord.

steps.label: Riot in the theater
steps.copy: Silversmiths who make shrines of Artemis stir the city into a riot.

steps.label: Through Macedonia
steps.copy: After the uproar, Paul travels through Macedonia, encouraging the believers.

steps.label: Three months in Greece
steps.copy: A plot against him makes him decide to go back through Macedonia.

steps.label: Philippi
steps.copy: After the Feast of Unleavened Bread, they sail from Philippi.

steps.label: Troas
steps.copy: Paul talks until midnight. Eutychus falls from a third-story window and is picked up dead; Paul embraces him, and he is taken home alive.

steps.label: Assos
steps.copy: Paul goes on foot while the others sail, and they meet him at Assos.

steps.label: Mitylene
steps.copy: They take him on board and come to Mitylene.

steps.label: Farewell at Miletus
steps.copy: Past Chios and Samos, he calls the Ephesian elders and says a tearful goodbye.

steps.label: Patara
steps.copy: By way of Cos and Rhodes they reach Patara and find a ship crossing to Phoenicia.

steps.label: Tyre
steps.copy: Passing Cyprus, they land at Tyre, where the disciples urge Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.

steps.label: Ptolemais
steps.copy: They greet the brothers and stay with them for a day.

steps.label: Caesarea
steps.copy: They stay with Philip the evangelist. Agabus binds his own hands and feet with Paul's belt as a warning.

steps.label: Jerusalem
steps.copy: The brothers welcome them warmly.

set.note: Every port Acts 27-28 names is shown. The storm drift to Malta is drawn as a single line; ancient sailing depended on season and wind.

steps.label: Setting sail
steps.copy: Paul, a prisoner in the care of the centurion Julius, boards a ship from Adramyttium.

steps.label: Sidon
steps.copy: Julius kindly lets Paul visit his friends.

steps.label: Myra
steps.copy: Sailing in the shelter of Cyprus, they reach Myra and change to a ship from Alexandria bound for Italy.

steps.label: Cnidus
steps.copy: They make slow headway against the wind.

steps.label: Fair Havens
steps.copy: Sailing under Crete, Paul warns that the voyage will end in disaster, but the centurion follows the pilot and the owner instead.

steps.label: Storm and shipwreck
steps.copy: A northeaster drives the ship for fourteen days until it runs aground, and all 276 people reach land safely.

steps.label: Malta
steps.copy: A viper bites Paul without harm, and he heals the father of Publius and many others on the island.

steps.label: Syracuse
steps.copy: After three months they sail on an Alexandrian ship with the Twin Brothers as its figurehead.

steps.label: Rhegium
steps.copy: They sail on to Rhegium.

steps.label: Puteoli
steps.copy: They find brothers there and stay with them seven days.

steps.label: Rome
steps.copy: Believers come out as far as the Forum of Appius and Three Taverns to meet him. In Rome he lives under guard and boldly proclaims the kingdom of God.
